summary:
FIREGUARD is an AI-powered space fire intelligence platform designed to make NASA spacecraft combustion research more accessible, searchable, and useful for future space mission planning. It transforms structured experimental data into an interactive research environment where users can explore investigations, compare experimental conditions and results, analyze mission relevance, and identify gaps in available research.

The platform combines a React-based interface, Node.js and Express backend, MongoDB database, and an evidence-grounded AI research assistant. Its features include a NASA investigation explorer, side-by-side experiment comparison, mission relevance analysis, and research gap identification. The AI assistant retrieves relevant stored evidence and provides source-linked answers while explicitly identifying missing information rather than inventing scientific findings.

FIREGUARD addresses the challenge of connecting fragmented experimental research with practical space exploration needs. By organizing combustion evidence and highlighting limitations in existing datasets, it can support researchers and mission planners in investigating spacecraft fire safety, material behavior, and areas requiring further experimentation.
details:
FIREGUARD is an AI-powered space fire intelligence platform designed to make spacecraft combustion research more accessible and useful for future space missions.

The platform organizes NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) research into a searchable database and provides an interactive interface for exploring investigations, comparing experimental conditions, asking research questions, analyzing mission relevance, and identifying gaps in available data.

Its main features include a Mission Control Dashboard, Investigation Explorer, AI Research Assistant, Experiment Comparator, Mission Analyzer, and Research Gaps module.

The AI assistant uses evidence retrieved from the curated database to generate source-supported responses. When sufficient evidence is unavailable, it communicates that limitation instead of inventing scientific findings. The mission analyzer uses a transparent, project-defined heuristic rather than a NASA-validated fire-risk prediction model.

We developed FIREGUARD using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and Mongoose, with a Gemini API integration attempt and a grounded fallback mechanism.

The project focuses on scientific transparency, traceability, and usability. Its intended impact is to help researchers and mission planners explore existing combustion evidence, compare experiments more efficiently, and identify areas where additional research may be needed.
